evals.expected_output: The skill should identify: (1) N+1 query problem — the nested loops produce O(orders * items) database queries; fix with JOIN or batch fetch. (2) Full table scan — `SELECT * FROM products` loads every product just to filter 5; fix with a WHERE clause using IN or a category join. (3) Repeated category lookup — `[prod['category'] for prod in products]` rebuilt on every iteration — O(n²); hoist to a set. (4) SELECT * — fetch only needed columns. Should quantify the worst-case: if 10 orders × 5 items each = 50+ queries per page load. Should suggest: SQL JOIN to collapse to 2-3 queries, add indexes on foreign keys, cache recommendations.
assertions: Identified the N+1 query pattern in the nested order/item loops
Quantified worst-case query count as orders × items (e.g., 10 orders × 5 items = 50+ queries per page load)
Identified the full-table-scan on SELECT * FROM products loaded entirely to filter 5 recommendations
Recommended indexing on foreign keys (user_id on orders, order_id on order_items, product_id on order_items)

evals.prompt: Our API endpoint takes 4-8 seconds to respond under load. We suspect it's slow but we don't know where. We have no profiling set up. Walk me through a systematic approach to finding and fixing the bottleneck.
evals.expected_output: The skill should give a structured profiling approach: (1) measure first — add timing instrumentation at coarse level (request in → DB calls → external APIs → response out) before guessing. (2) Identify the bottleneck category: CPU-bound (algorithm, hot path), I/O-bound (DB, external API, disk), or memory-bound (GC pressure, allocation). (3) For each category, specific tools/techniques: cProfile/py-spy for CPU, slow query log + EXPLAIN for DB, distributed tracing for API chains. (4) The 80/20 rule — fix the slowest 20% first, re-measure, repeat. Should explicitly say 'don't optimize without measuring' and 'don't fix what the profiler didn't flag'.
assertions: Recommended measuring/profiling before guessing or attempting any fix
Identified the three bottleneck categories: CPU-bound, I/O-bound, and memory-bound
Named at least two specific profiling tools (e.g., cProfile, py-spy, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, clinic.js, pprof)
Applied the 80/20 rule — fix the biggest bottleneck first, re-measure, then repeat

evals.prompt: We're running a real-time leaderboard that updates every 5 seconds. Our stack: Node.js API, PostgreSQL, Redis. The leaderboard has 1M users. Our current approach: on every update, we recalculate the full leaderboard with SELECT user_id, SUM(score) FROM events GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 100 running against a 500M-row events table. We're seeing 15-second query times. We also have 50 Node workers all doing this calculation simultaneously every 5 seconds. Where are the bottlenecks and what's the fix?
evals.expected_output: The skill should identify: (1) Aggregate query on 500M rows is the core problem — the events table needs to be materialized or pre-aggregated; maintain a scores table updated incrementally on each event insert rather than recalculating the full sum on every read. (2) 50 workers doing the same calculation every 5s = fan-out of 50 identical expensive queries simultaneously — replace with a single background job that recalculates and pushes to Redis; workers read from cache instead of hitting PostgreSQL. (3) ORDER BY on a non-indexed computed column at 1M users is O(n log n) sort on every request. (4) Recommend: Redis sorted set (ZADD/ZREVRANGE is O(log n) per update, O(k) read for top-k); update scores incrementally on event insert; workers read ZREVRANGE from Redis rather than querying PostgreSQL.
assertions: Identified the 500M-row aggregate query as the primary bottleneck (full table scan recalculated on every update)
Recommended Redis sorted sets (ZADD/ZREVRANGE) or equivalent pre-aggregation strategy
Flagged the 50-worker fan-out as unnecessary duplication of the same expensive query
Recommended incremental score updates on event insert instead of recalculating full aggregates
